The French Revolution (1789-1799) - Revision Sheet
History 201. Causes, timeline, key figures, vocabulary.

1. Long-term Causes
Financial crisis: decades of war debt (including support for the
American Revolution) plus an unfair tax system.
Social structure: the Three Estates - clergy (1st), nobility (2nd),
everyone else (3rd, about 97% of the population, paying most taxes).
Enlightenment ideas: Rousseau, Voltaire and Montesquieu questioned
absolute monarchy and promoted popular sovereignty.

2. Timeline
May 1789: Estates-General convenes at Versailles for the first time
since 1614. June 1789: Third Estate declares itself the National
Assembly (Tennis Court Oath).
July 14, 1789: Storming of the Bastille - the symbolic start.
August 1789: Declaration of the Rights of Man and of the Citizen.
1791: First constitution; Louis XVI's failed Flight to Varennes.
1792: Monarchy abolished; First Republic proclaimed.
January 1793: Execution of Louis XVI by guillotine.
1793-1794: Reign of Terror under Robespierre and the Committee of
Public Safety - about 17,000 official executions.
July 1794: Thermidorian Reaction - Robespierre falls and is executed.
1795-1799: The Directory, a five-man executive, rules unstable France.
November 1799: Napoleon's coup of 18 Brumaire ends the Revolution.

3. Key Figures
Louis XVI: king executed in 1793. Marie Antoinette: queen, executed
the same year. Robespierre: architect of the Terror. Danton: early
revolutionary leader, later guillotined. Napoleon Bonaparte: general
who seized power in 1799.

4. Vocabulary
Bastille: royal fortress-prison in Paris. Guillotine: execution
device adopted as a 'humane' method. Sans-culottes: radical working
class militants. Emigres: nobles who fled abroad. Jacobins: the
radical political club that dominated the Terror.

5. Exam Prompts
Q1. Was the Terror a defence of the Revolution or a betrayal of it?
Q2. Compare the roles of the Estates-General and the National
Assembly in triggering the Revolution.
